prompt: Tag 3 million product descriptions with categories. Results are needed by next week, and cost matters more than speed.
why: Submit them through a batch API: asynchronous, higher throughput, typically about half the price.
trap: Routing lowers per-call cost too, but the offline deadline is the bigger lever.

prompt: Every night, summarize all of the day's 200,000 support tickets for a morning report.
why: A large offline job with hours of slack: batch it.
trap: Nobody is waiting on any single summary, so real-time calls are wasted.

prompt: You switched embedding models and must re-embed 40 million documents without hitting your real-time rate limits.
tells: without hitting your real-time rate limits
why: Run the backfill as batch jobs with their own quota, separate from live traffic.
trap: It's for a RAG system, but the task at hand is a big offline job.

prompt: Run 50,000 test prompts against three candidate models over the weekend as cheaply as possible.
tells: over the weekend as cheaply as possible
why: The evaluation itself is the goal, but running it cheaply over a weekend is batch inference.
trap: Evals is the purpose; the question here is how to run that many calls cheaply.

prompt: A provider offers 50% off for requests that can wait up to 24 hours. You have 500,000 documents to classify for a quarterly audit.
why: Offline, deadline-flexible bulk work fits a batch API.
trap: Nobody is waiting on each answer, so trade latency for cost.

prompt: Generate 200,000 synthetic Q&A pairs from your docs to train a smaller model next month.
why: Data generation at scale with no live user is batch work.
trap: The end goal is fine-tuning, but this step is a batch job.

prompt: A script looping over 1 million rows calling the chat API keeps hitting rate limits and takes days.
why: Submit a batch job; it has separate, higher limits and handles queuing for you.
trap: Retries with backoff help, but the batch API is designed for this.

prompt: Translate a 10-year archive of 2 million help articles into Spanish before a market launch in 6 weeks.
why: Large, non-interactive, with a generous deadline: batch it.
trap: Speed per request doesn't matter here.
